page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a cloud compute instance in the High Performance family, configured with 12 shared virtual CPUs across 6 physical Intel Xeon cores at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 24.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per thread. Storage is provisioned through an integrated 500 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. Processor capabilities include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI vector instruction support, alongside AES cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded operations, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 17934.88 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 17309.27. In contrast, per-thread computational velocity is moderate, with Geekbench single-core testing scoring 1036.0. Memory throughput remains balanced, sustaining 87.74 GB/sec read and 47.62 GB/sec write rates on large uncached blocks. In application testing, the system handles 18.53 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers 11.99 GB/sec of static web serving throughput, while larger neural model inference is constrained by the absence of discrete GPU hardware.

The combination of 12 compute threads and local NVMe storage delivers resource density for multi-process environments without requiring external volume attachments. The instance profile is suited for concurrent web serving, software build pipelines, intermediate database services, and Redis in-memory caching tiers. Environments dependent on extreme single-thread frequency or higher RAM-per-core allocations may require dedicated-core or memory-optimized alternatives.
